title: Sound Distributed Runtime Verification with Incomplete Evidence: A Balanced Search Indexing Approach
topic: Sound Distributed Runtime Verification under Incomplete Evidence
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: Distributed systems frequently emit partial event streams, making runtime verification of safety properties challenging. We present a Java-based verification engine that aggregates events into a height-balanced binary search tree, enabling sound inference of property satisfaction even when evidence is incomplete. The engine guarantees that each insertion or query executes in $O(\log N)$ time, where $N$ is the number of distinct predicates observed, and that the tree remains strictly height-balanced and key-ordered. Formal invariants are proven using a structural induction over the tree nodes, and static analysis confirms the absence of race conditions in the event-processing pipeline. The implementation is fully open-source and available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/java-enterprise-patterns/tree/main/algorithms/20261125_170139_sound_distributed_runtime_veri}. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/java-enterprise-patterns/tree/main/algorithms/20261125_170139_sound_distributed_runtime_veri}
